claim: Did OSHA have a rule on tornado shelters for large buildings in 2021?
value: No. No OSHA standard requires severe-weather plans; OSHA recommends them under the General Duty Clause
verbatim_quote: OSHA does not have a standard that requires severe weather emergency plans but recommends them
note: Strongest primary source for "no rule". Quote is OSHA saying so after the fact. General Emergency Action Plan standard 29 CFR 1910.38 exists but is not tornado-specific (my knowledge, not sourced here).

value: FEMA P-361 is for community and residential safe rooms (current 5th ed. Nov 2024, on ICC 500-2023). FEMA P-320 covers sites sheltering 16 or fewer. Edwardsville code asked only for 90 mph winds; no shelter required
